question: What was the staff's fear about the new rule?
options: That books would not be returned
That the library would become crowded
That the register would be lost

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: When a town library introduced a rule that books could be borrowed without a card, some staff feared that many books would never come back. The librarian decided to test the idea for one year. Borrowers only had to write their name and phone number in a register. To everyone's surprise, the number of missing books hardly changed, while the number of borrowers almost doubled. Many new readers were students and daily-wage workers who had found the card process too slow. The librarian concluded that most people respond to trust with responsibility, and that rules meant to prevent a few losses can keep many honest people away.
